_readme: Device profiles for MediaPorter v2. Edit this file to add or correct a device -
it is read at startup, no rebuild needed.
width/height  the encode target. For small screens this is the panel itself;
for phones big enough to show it, a standard 720p/1080p box.
fpsCap        source frame rate is PRESERVED and only capped at this value.
profile/level H.264 profile and level the device is documented to decode.
maxRate       ceiling for the quality-targeted encode, not a fixed bitrate.
audioBitrate  AAC-LC, kept at or under what the device accepts.
hevc          true only where HEVC hardware decode is certain (A9 and later).
Ignored unless HEVC is switched on in the device picker.
video         false = the device plays no video at all (listed for reference,
cannot be picked as a video target). Music works on all of them.
verified      true = taken from Apple's own tech-spec page for that model.
false = derived from the same-generation model that was verified.
Erring low is safe (slightly softer picture). Erring high is not - a file above
what the decoder accepts simply refuses to play.

devices.name: iPod nano (7th gen)
devices.note: The last nano. Encodes to the panel exactly; High profile is the best of the three it accepts.

devices.name: iPod nano (5th gen)
devices.note: 2.2-inch screen, the widest of the small nanos.

devices.name: iPod nano (4th gen)
devices.note: 2-inch screen, portrait panel used landscape for video.

devices.name: iPod nano (3rd gen)
devices.note: The first nano that played video.

devices.name: iPod classic (6th gen / 120-160GB)
devices.note: Accepts up to 640x480 for TV-out, but the panel is 320x240 - that is what it shows.

devices.name: iPod (5th gen, 'iPod video')
devices.note: The strictest profile in the whole range: Baseline level 1.3, hard ceiling of 768 kbps.

devices.name: iPod touch (7th gen)
devices.note: A10 chip - hardware HEVC, so it can take the smaller files if you switch HEVC on.

devices.name: iPod touch (6th gen)
devices.note: A8 chip.

devices.name: iPod touch (5th gen)
devices.note: Apple documents Main profile 3.1 here, not High - so this one stays on Main.

devices.name: iPod touch (4th gen)
devices.note: First Retina touch.

devices.name: iPod touch (1st - 3rd gen)
devices.note: Pre-Retina touch.

devices.name: iPhone X and later (X, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16)
devices.note: Full 1080p. These will happily play the source untouched - transcoding is only worth it to save space.

devices.name: iPhone 6 Plus - 8 Plus
devices.note: 1080p panel. HEVC from the 6s Plus onward (A9).

devices.name: iPhone 6 - 8, SE (2nd/3rd gen)
devices.note: 720p is the natural fit for a 1334x750 panel. HEVC from the 6s onward (A9).

devices.name: iPhone 5, 5c, 5s, SE (1st gen)
devices.note: 4-inch panel.

devices.name: iPhone 4, 4S
devices.note: First Retina iPhone.

devices.name: iPhone, 3G, 3GS
devices.note: Same panel and limits as the early iPod touch.

devices.name: iPad Pro (all), Air 3+, iPad 5th gen+, mini 5+
devices.note: A9 and later, so HEVC is available if you switch it on. These play a 1080p source untouched - transcoding only saves space.

devices.name: iPad Air, Air 2, iPad mini 2 / 3 / 4
devices.note: 1080p at 60 fps, High profile 4.2. A7/A8 chips - no HEVC.

devices.name: iPad (3rd / 4th gen)
devices.note: First Retina iPads. 1080p, but 30 fps rather than 60.

devices.name: iPad 2, iPad mini (1st gen)
devices.note: Decodes 1080p High 4.1 but the panel is only 1024x768 - so it is encoded to fit the screen, not the decoder.

devices.name: iPad (1st gen)
devices.note: The only iPad limited to Main profile 3.1 and 720p; the iPad 2 jumped straight to High 4.1.

devices.name: iPod nano (6th gen)
devices.family: Music only - these cannot play video
devices.note: The square clip-on nano. Apple's spec sheet lists no video formats at all - it plays music, radio and photos only. Music downloads work on it exactly like every other device here.

devices.name: iPod nano (1st / 2nd gen)
devices.family: Music only - these cannot play video
devices.note: Screen too small for video; the nano only gained playback with the 3rd gen.

devices.name: iPod (1st - 4th gen), mini, photo
devices.family: Music only - these cannot play video
devices.note: Everything before the 5th gen. The photo model shows stills but plays no video.

devices.name: iPod shuffle (all generations)
devices.family: Music only - these cannot play video
devices.note: No screen at all.
